skill.name: entra-app-registration
skill.description: Guides secure Microsoft Entra ID app registration, OAuth flow selection, API permissions, Azure CLI configuration, and MSAL integration.
skill.summary: Configure Microsoft Entra applications with secure authentication and least-privilege access.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are lexical false positives caused by Markdown, Microsoft endpoints, OAuth scopes, and explicit Azure administration examples. Confirmed risks include unsafe placeholder redirects, credential-reset commands, and an unguarded cleanup loop. Semantic review also found a source-embedded secret pattern, broad default Graph permissions, and overbroad public-client guidance.

remediation.issue: The Node.js example places a client secret in source code.
remediation.suggestion: Load secrets from managed identity, Key Vault, or a protected runtime secret provider. Show no source-level secret assignment.

remediation.issue: The Bicep template requests broad Graph permissions by default.
remediation.suggestion: Default to User.Read only. Parameterize additional permissions and require documented approval before adding application roles.

remediation.issue: Examples register non-reserved placeholder redirect and logout domains.
remediation.suggestion: Require redirect parameters without external defaults. Validate ownership and HTTPS before creating or updating an app registration.

remediation.issue: Credential creation examples reset and remove existing credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Use --append for staged rotation. Verify the new credential before removing the old credential by key ID.

remediation.issue: The cleanup loop deletes every application returned by a broad name match.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry run, exact allowlist, per-application confirmation, and tenant verification before deletion.

remediation.issue: The beginner guide enables public client flows for every console application.
remediation.suggestion: Enable only the required flow. Do not enable resource owner password flow, and prefer authorization code with PKCE or device code.

semantic_findings.title: Client Secret Embedded in Source Example
semantic_findings.description: The Node.js example places the client secret directly in source configuration. Users who replace the placeholder may commit a live credential to version control.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The clientSecret field is explicitly populated from an app-registration placeholder inside source code. The surrounding example provides no secure retrieval pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Overprivileged Default API Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The deployable Bicep example requests Mail.Read and application-level User.Read.All by default. An approved deployment can expose mailbox and directory data beyond basic sign-in needs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permission IDs and comments directly configure delegated mail access and tenant-wide application user access. These permissions are unrelated to a minimal registration baseline.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Public Client Flow Enablement
semantic_findings.description: The beginner guide tells every console app to enable public client flows, including resource owner password flow. This expands the authentication surface without confirming the required flow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly identifies resource owner password flow and directs console-app users to enable the setting. It does not limit the advice to device-code requirements.

content.user_title: Configure Secure Microsoft Entra App Registrations
content.value_statement: Identity setup errors can expose data, break sign-in, or grant excessive access. This skill guides Entra registration, OAuth selection, permissions, credentials, and MSAL integration.
actual_capabilities: Explains Entra application types, identifiers, redirect URIs, service principals, and credentials.
Guides portal and Azure CLI workflows for creating and updating app registrations.
Compares authorization code, PKCE, client credentials, device code, and refresh token flows.
Maps delegated and application permissions to consent requirements and Microsoft Graph identifiers.
Provides MSAL examples for .NET, Python, and Node.js console applications.
Troubleshoots common Entra errors involving redirects, consent, tenants, secrets, and service principals.
limitations: Requires tenant access and appropriate Entra roles for registration, consent, and credential operations.
Does not replace organizational identity architecture, threat modeling, or production security review.
Example identifiers, domains, permissions, and secrets must be replaced and validated before use.
Does not manage Azure RBAC assignments or audit Key Vault expiration.

use_cases.title: Register a first application
use_cases.description: Choose account types, redirect URIs, delegated permissions, and a suitable interactive OAuth flow.

use_cases.title: Automate tenant configuration
use_cases.description: Prepare reviewed Azure CLI or Bicep steps for repeatable app registration and service-principal setup.

use_cases.title: Review access and consent
use_cases.description: Compare requested Graph permissions with business needs and identify permissions requiring administrator consent.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first registration plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through registering a [application type] named [name]. Ask for missing redirect URIs, account types, and required permissions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup through the Entra portal

prompt_templates.title: Select an OAuth flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend the safest OAuth flow for [application architecture]. Explain required Entra settings, token handling, and why other flows are less suitable.
prompt_templates.scenario: Authentication design for a new application

prompt_templates.title: Prepare reviewed CLI steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare Azure CLI steps for [application name] using [redirect URIs] and [permissions]. Include verification, least privilege, and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an advanced Entra design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Entra design: [details]. Identify excessive permissions, unsafe redirects, credential risks, consent requirements, and production-ready MSAL changes.

output_examples.input: Register a single-tenant web application with one callback and basic profile access.
output: Redirect review: verify ownership and require HTTPS.
Credential choice: managed identity or certificate for production.

output_examples.input: Choose authentication for a desktop application that cannot keep a secret.
output_examples.output: Use authorization code with PKCE and a verified loopback redirect. Register it as a public client and do not create a client secret.
Compare the requested and registered redirect URIs exactly, including scheme, host, path, case, trailing slash, and platform type.

best_practices: Start with minimal delegated permissions and document every permission increase.
Use managed identity or workload identity in production, with deterministic credential selection.
Verify redirect ownership, tenant context, and affected objects before applying administrative commands.
anti_patterns: Do not place client secrets, certificates, or access tokens in source files or chat prompts.
Do not grant tenant-wide application permissions when delegated access meets the requirement.
Do not run credential reset, consent, or deletion commands without impact review and rollback steps.

faq.question: Can this skill create an Entra app automatically?
faq.answer: It can prepare portal, Azure CLI, or Bicep guidance. Execution still requires authenticated tenant access and appropriate roles.

faq.question: Which OAuth flow should a public client use?
faq.answer: Prefer authorization code with PKCE. Device code is suitable when the device cannot open a browser.

faq.question: When is administrator consent required?
faq.answer: All application permissions and some privileged delegated permissions require administrator consent. Tenant policy may require consent for additional scopes.

faq.question: Should production applications use client secrets?
faq.answer: Prefer managed identity, workload identity, or certificates. When secrets are unavoidable, store and rotate them through a protected secret service.

faq.question: Does this skill cover Azure RBAC?
faq.answer: No. It covers Entra app registration and API permissions, not Azure resource role assignments.

faq.question: Can examples be used without changes?
faq.answer: No. Replace placeholders, minimize permissions, verify domains, review tenant impact, and test in a non-production environment first.
